blocks.content: Stars are self-luminous celestial bodies that produce immense light and heat energy through continuous nuclear fusion at their cores.

rows: Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium
Appear stationary relative to each other
Revolve around stars in defined orbits

items: Light-year is a unit of astronomical distance, NOT a unit of time.
The Chandrasekhar Limit (1.44 Solar Masses) defines the maximum mass threshold for a stable White Dwarf.
Planets do not twinkle like stars because they are closer to Earth and act as extended sources of light.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Stars are massive self-luminous celestial bodies composed mainly of Hydrogen and Helium undergoing nuclear fusion.
The Sun is the closest star to Earth, situated at an average distance of approximately 150 million kilometers.
Distances between stars are measured in light-years, which is the distance light travels in one Julian year at 300,000 km/s.
The Pole Star (Polaris) appears stationary in the sky because it lies directly above the Earth's rotational north pole.
Stars twinkle when observed from Earth due to continuous atmospheric refraction caused by air temperature and density fluctuations.
